blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Any proposal to tax coffee products is already considered “dead on arrival” at the House of Representatives, Marikina Rep. Miro Quimbo said on Thursday. In a message to reporters, Quimbo said coffee cannot be subjected to an excise tax because such policy is primarily imposed on products to discourage consumption behaviors that may be harmful to health, such as smoking and excessive alcohol drinking. “We have rejected it. Dead on arrival at the HOR (House of Representatives),” said Quimbo, chairperson of the House committee on ways and means, which deliberates on tax proposals. “Excise taxes are meant to curb a […]...
